1.why: All MFA endpoints resolve the user solely from the server-side session via authorized(), and invalidIdentifierAttempt() rejects any client-supplied userId/accountId/ownerId, so settings are bound to the signed-in user.

2.why: Verification is checked against the session-bound user's own encrypted provision secret (with the manualSecret required to match and usedSteps preventing replay), so a code cannot be used across users; the statement is false.

3.why: verify-authenticator sets mfaActive=true without deleting or rotating entries in the sessions map, so any previously issued sessions remain valid after MFA is enabled.

4.why: The OTP secret is stored AES-GCM encrypted (encryptSecret) and backup codes are stored as peppered SHA-256 hashes, never in plain text.

5.why: All secrets, tokens, recovery codes, the master key and pepper are generated with crypto.getRandomValues, a CSPRNG.

6.why: Session and pre-auth cookies are HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict and the client script keeps all secrets in an in-memory state object with no localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookie use.

7.why: Server-side validators validEmail, validPhone, validOtp, validSecret and validRecovery are applied to every user-supplied field before processing.

8.why: Dynamic values (secret, codes, server messages) are inserted exclusively via textContent, and innerHTML is used only with static template strings, preventing script execution.

9.why: safeInternalPath restricts the 'next' destination to a fixed allow-list of internal hash routes and defaults to #/dashboard otherwise.

10.why: standardHeaders sets HSTS, CSP (with frame-ancestors 'none'), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, plus Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy on every response.

11.why: sessionCookie emits 'mfa_session=...; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict' with all three required attributes.

12.why: Server-side there are no secret logs, generic errors and no stack traces, but the client mockLog writes the OTP seed, current OTP and backup codes to console.log and a persistent on-page log panel, so secrets are not fully kept out of logs.

13.why: TOTPs are bound to the current 30-second step with usedSteps blocking reuse, provisioning expires after 15 minutes, and recovery codes are deleted from the backups array upon successful use.

14.why: recordFailure enforces a 10-minute lockout after 5 failed attempts for login, authenticator verification and recovery verification, plus a 60-second throttle on backup regeneration.

15.why: Login deletes any prior session and issues a fresh random ID (rotation), sessions enforce 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts in getSession, and logout deletes the session server-side and clears the cookie.
